site.name: Civic Leb
site.about: We cannot govern systems we do not understand. Civic Leb is a complete data model of the Lebanese state: bodies, positions, the people who hold them, and the legal relationships between them, each cited to its source.
site.builtBy: An open project. Code MIT, data CC BY.
site.metaDescription: A map of the Lebanese state: every institution and office, who holds it, and the law that links them. Who appoints whom, who oversees whom, which posts are allocated by confession.

edgeHelp.elects: The first body chooses the holders of the second by vote.
edgeHelp.appoints: The first body names the holders of the second, usually by decree.
edgeHelp.confirms: The first body must grant its confidence or approval for the second to take office or act.
edgeHelp.dept_head: The position is the institutional head of this body.
edgeHelp.ex_officio: The holder of the first position sits on the second body by virtue of office, without a separate appointment.
edgeHelp.oversees: The first body supervises, audits or holds the second to account.
edgeHelp.advises: The first body gives non-binding opinions to the second.
edgeHelp.administers: The first body has authority over the running of the second.
edgeHelp.office: An office attached to the body.
edgeHelp.tutelage: Administrative tutelage: the ministry approves the institution's budget, board and major decisions and proposes its appointments.
edgeHelp.owns: The first body holds the shares of the second.
edgeHelp.inspects: The first body may inspect the second's administration and finances.
edgeHelp.prosecutes: The first body brings cases before the second.
edgeHelp.reviews: The first body reviews the second's acts or laws and may annul them.
edgeHelp.commands: The holder of the first position is commander-in-chief of the second.
edgeHelp.regulates: The first body licenses, regulates and sanctions the second.
edgeHelp.disciplines: The first body may discipline the members of the second.
edgeHelp.refers_to: The first body refers cases to the second.
